env: A stock RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell host with two GPUs, Docker, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, NGC credentials, and the VSS repository at `{{repo_root}}`. Covers VDR row 2, "Use the vss-build-vision-ai skill to add real-time VLM alerting and summarization". Step 1 stands up the base vision agent so step 2 has a running deployment to extend, and declares `artifact_expected: false` because the graded build artifact is the extended one step 2 writes. Two GPUs because real-time alerting runs continuous RT-VLM alongside the LLM the in-stack agent already needs; the base profile alone fits on one.

expects.query: Use `/vss-build-vision-ai` to deploy a vision agent on `{{platform}}` from `{{repo_root}}`. Deploy the stock `base` pre-built developer workflow with its authoritative service set unchanged, write the build artifacts under `_builds/vdr-2-base/`, validate the resolved Compose file, and leave the deployment running. Bring the stack up with a detached `docker compose ... up -d` from the validated `resolved.yml` as soon as validation passes; do not spend the trial budget on a separate blocking image pull first - let first-boot pulls finish in the background while polling readiness. This build uses the in-stack agent: deploy `vss-agent` and its Web UI as part of the service set and do not substitute a host-side harness, so harness selection does not apply. Run autonomously and non-interactively: this trial has no interactive user, so do not pause for deployment confirmation at any point.
checks: `{{repo_root}}/_builds/vdr-2-base/override.env` exists and declares `FOUNDATION=base` and the full effective `COMPOSE_PROFILES`.
The deployment is launched directly from `_builds/vdr-2-base/resolved.yml` after validation.
`curl -sf --max-time 15 http://localhost:8000/health` returns exit 0 (Agent REST API responsive).
`docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx vss-agent` returns exit 0.

The effective service set carries no alerting or summarization keys yet: `COMPOSE_PROFILES` contains neither `alert-bridge` nor `lvs-server`, so step 2 has a real delta to compute.

expects.query: Now take the vision agent down and add VLM alerting and video summarization to my deployment. Use `/vss-build-vision-ai`, treat the deployment from the previous step as the starting point, tear it down, and bring the extended build up in its place under `_builds/vdr-2-alerting-summarization/`. Keep the in-stack agent: `vss-agent` and its Web UI stay in the service set and no host-side harness is substituted, so harness selection does not apply. Validate the resolved Compose file, then bring the stack up with a detached `docker compose ... up -d` as soon as validation passes and leave it running for readiness checks; do not spend the trial budget on a separate blocking image pull first. Run autonomously and non-interactively: this trial has no interactive user, so do not pause for deployment confirmation at any point and do not ask which capabilities are meant - real-time VLM alerting and video summarization are both requested.
checks: The previous deployment is torn down before the extended build is brought up: the trajectory runs a `docker compose ... down` against the step-1 project rather than leaving two projects running or starting a second stack alongside the first.

`{{repo_root}}/_builds/vdr-2-alerting-summarization/override.env` exists, declares a `FOUNDATION` that is one of the current developer profiles, and carries the full effective `COMPOSE_PROFILES` for the extended build.

The build is expressed as a delta on exactly one current developer Foundation: only canonical service-profile keys are added, and no invented `vdr-2-alerting-summarization` or aggregate profile key appears in `COMPOSE_PROFILES`.
The effective service set adds real-time alerting: `COMPOSE_PROFILES` includes `alert-bridge` and `vss-video-analytics-api`, together with the Kafka and Elasticsearch peers `alert-bridge` requires.
The effective service set adds video summarization: `COMPOSE_PROFILES` includes `lvs-server`.
The effective service set keeps continuous RT-VLM for VLM-based alerting and keeps the in-stack agent and its Web UI - `vss-agent` is not dropped in favour of a host-side harness.
`{{repo_root}}/_builds/vdr-2-alerting-summarization/` contains `override.env`, `compose.yml`, and `resolved.yml`, and the deployment is launched directly from that `resolved.yml` after validation.
`curl -sf --max-time 15 http://localhost:8000/health` returns exit 0 (Agent REST API responsive).
`docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx vss-agent` returns exit 0.
`docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx vss-alert-bridge` returns exit 0 (real-time VLM alerting).
`docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx vss-lvs` returns exit 0 (video summarization service).
`docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx vss-rtvi-vlm` returns exit 0 (RT-VLM still serving after the rebuild).
`curl -sf --max-time 15 http://localhost:38111/v1/ready` returns exit 0 (LVS summarization API responsive).
The final response names both added capabilities in the build's own terms and states that the earlier deployment was replaced rather than left running alongside.
